en: The Makahiya plant rapidly folds its leaves when touched to protect itself from hungry insects.
A carabao cools its body by wallowing in mud because it lacks sweat glands.
When you exhale on a cold morning, the water vapor in your breath condenses into visible fog.
The caterpillar of the Common Rose butterfly forms a green chrysalis before emerging as an adult.
Mangrove trees grow specialized above-ground roots called pneumatophores to absorb oxygen in waterlogged coastal soils.
The Tokay gecko uses specialized toe pads with microscopic hairs to climb smooth vertical surfaces.
The fibrous husk of a coconut allows the fruit to float across the ocean for dispersal.
Male fireflies produce bioluminescent light from their abdomens to attract mates during warm summer nights.
Only female Aedes aegypti mosquitoes bite humans to obtain protein needed for developing their eggs.
Water lilies have wide, flat leaves with stomata on the upper surface to float and photosynthesize.
The Maya bird builds a dome-shaped nest with a side entrance to protect its eggs from predators.
Banana plants reproduce asexually by growing new shoots called suckers from their underground rhizomes.
